alignments.note: Subject pronoun with the verb; *up* restates the direction the clause writes and belongs to the English phrasal verb (rule 44).
Accusative of direction with the preposition the ASV supplies for its case-function (rule 33).
Adverbial predicate of a verbless clause takes the construction-supplied copula (rule 20).
Explicit subject pronoun takes only its own English (rule 20).
Waw rendered by the connective *If* (rule 14; the corpus aligns a waw to *if*).
Light verb plus complement: head on *bed* (rule 44), the unit discontinuous around the supplied possessive.
Supplied possessive with no suffix or other possessive morpheme in the clause (rule 18's closing sentence); it is not made the verb's by the noun beside it (rule 44).
Bare locative nominal with the preposition supplied for its case-function (rule 33).

Presentative particle takes its *behold* together with the copula and deictic *there* the construction supplies for this second colon, which writes no שָׁם (rules 20, 21). Marking *there* `added` was the competing reading.
Suffix on the particle rendered by the subject pronoun.
